written.q: Explain how a timer generates a PWM waveform and derive the PWM frequency and duty cycle for fast PWM.
written.a: The prescaled clock increments TCNT from 0 to TOP. A comparator compares TCNT with OCRnX; at the match the waveform generator clears the OCnX pin (non-inverted) and it is set again when TCNT returns to 0. FPWM = F_CPU / ((TOP + 1) × prescale); duty cycle = (OCR + 1) / (TOP + 1). With TOP = 255, prescale 64 and F_CPU = 16 MHz, FPWM = 976.6 Hz; OCR = 127 gives 50 %.

written.q: Compare fast PWM and phase correct PWM.
written.a: Fast PWM counts up only then jumps to 0 (frequency F_CPU/(256×prescale), edge aligned, highest frequency). Phase correct PWM counts up and down (frequency F_CPU/(510×prescale), half of fast PWM), and its pulses are symmetric about the centre, which suits motor control; duty ≈ OCR/TOP.

written.q: Write the register configuration to produce 1 kHz non-inverted fast PWM on PD6 and explain each bit.
written.a:
DDRD |= (1<<DDD6);                       // PD6 output
TCCR0A = (1<<COM0A1)|(1<<WGM01)|(1<<WGM00); // non-inverted, fast PWM
TCCR0B = (1<<CS01)|(1<<CS00);              // /64 = 976.6 Hz
OCR0A = 128;                               // about 50 % duty

COM0A1:0 = 10 clears OC0A at the match; WGM02:0 = 011 is fast PWM; CS = 011 selects F_CPU/64.

written.q: Describe the auto fan design and the firmware logic.
written.a: LM35 on A0 with the 1.1 V reference (T = ADCW × 1.1/1024 × 100). PWM on pin 6 (OC0A) drives a BC547 or 2N7000 that switches the motor, with a 1N4001 flyback diode and a common ground. Duty: 0 at ≤ 25 °C, 255 at ≥ 35 °C and (T − 25)/10 × 255 between, written to OCR0A (or analogWrite(6, duty)).
